title: Staggered-region rollout schedule and fallout plan — WIP
content:
Status: WIP — operational schedule + contingency for a staggered multi-region rollout (no DB schema changes).

Summary:
This doc captures the operational schedule for a staggered regional rollout of v2.14 (serving runtime + routing changes) across Redwood Hosted regions. The approach: small canary in a single region, progressive ramp to multiple regions with guarded feature-flag gating, and an explicit fallout plan for service degradations. Goal is to minimize blast radius, preserve latency SLOs, and provide clear rollback/mitigation steps.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API model-serving changes that affect routing, batching heuristics, and kernel selection.
- Excludes any coordinated customer DB migrations or private deployment pushes.
- Targeted regions: us-west1, us-east4, eu-west1, asia-northeast1.

Objectives:
- Validate that runtime changes do not regress 95th/99th latency beyond +15% vs baseline.
- Ensure error rate (5xx) stays within 0.5x of baseline for canary windows.
- Verify CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth remain within operational thresholds.

Stakeholders and contact matrix:
- Release lead: Ethan Walker (owner) — primary decision authority during rollout
- SRE on-call: Priya Nair — infra & routing, rollback execution
- Serving runtime eng: Luca Romano — hotfixes and diagnostic builds
- Console & alerts: Aiko Tanaka — dashboards, incident comms
- Solutions / SE: Joanna King — customer outbound comms if customer-facing impact

High-level calendar (UTC times):
- Day -3 (2026-07-06): Final freeze of release artifacts, smoke-test infra in staging, ensure canary keys and rate-limits set.
- Day -1 (2026-07-08 18:00 UTC): Dry-run of canary promotion in staging; confirm dashboards and alert buckets.
- Day 0 (2026-07-09): Canary in us-west1
  - 08:00 UTC — Deploy runtime v2.14 to 2 canary nodes 
  - 08:10 — Start shifted traffic: 1% production (traffic split via routing-policy canary flag)
  - 08:10–09:40 — Canary observation window (100 min): metrics every 1m; escalation threshold if 5xx > baseline*1.5 or p99 latency > baseline*1.15
  - 09:45 — Promote to 5% if healthy; continue 3h observation windows per step
  - 13:00 — If stable, promote to 25%
  - 18:00 — 100% region completion (target)
- Day 1 (2026-07-10): us-east4 (repeat same cadence, start 08:00 UTC)
- Day 2 (2026-07-11): eu-west1
- Day 3 (2026-07-12): asia-northeast1 (note: start earlier in UTC to align local daytime ops)

Canary windows and acceptance criteria:
- Canary window durations: initial (100m), mid (3h), wide (6h).
- Acceptance metrics (all measured vs a 72h baseline):
  - 5xx rate: must not exceed 1.5x baseline during any 1m bucket; sustained spikes trigger immediate rollback
  - p50/p95/p99 latency: p99 must be <= baseline p99 * 1.15; p95 <= baseline * 1.10
  - Token-generation throughput: throughput should not drop more than 10% per node under same traffic mix
  - GPU memory and queue depth: no OOMs; queue depth growth >2x baseline for >10m triggers paging to alert channel
  - Error signatures: any new unknown 5xx signature requires triage with serving runtime lead

Traffic shaping and feature flags:
- Use routing-policy canary flag (route.rules.canary) to control percent-based split.
- Feature toggles: batching-optimizer=on (default off until region-wide full traffic), kv-cache-prefetch=experimental.
- If a regression is suspected, flip batching-optimizer=off for region to test impact quickly.

Rollback / Fallout plan (short form):
1) Pause promotions and stop further region rollouts.
2) If severe (5xx sustained, customer-impacting or p99 > threshold for >30m): full region rollback to previous runtime image.
3) Execute rollback steps (SRE lead):
   - Scale up previous image on dedicated rollback nodes, update routing policy to point region traffic to rollback nodes, ensure old cache warm-up as needed.
   - If rollback fails or partial traffic persists, cut traffic by routing policy to a healthy region (fallback-region routing) and open cross-region mitigation incident.
4) Post-rollback: capture heap/dump logs, collect traces (sampled), open incident ticket and tag release owner for postmortem.

Hotfix procedure:
- If root cause is isolated to a small code path and patch <= 3 commits: prepare hotfix branch, cut a hotfix candidate image, run a fast validation job in staging for 30–60m, then perform a 10% canary in the affected region with a 2h observation window.
- Hotfix must include deterministic repro steps and a rollback patch.

Monitoring & dashboards to watch (primary):
- release/routing/canary-summary (canary progress, per-region percent)
- infra/gpu-utilization/<region> (node-by-node)
- serving/latency/p50_p95_p99 (region filtered)
- errors/5xx-by-signature (top signatures)
- queuing/avg-depth (per inference-queue)
- business/failed-requests-customer-impacting (tracked per tenant)

Escalation playbook:
- Triage channel: #releases (SRE + Release lead + runtime lead pinned)
- If degraded: SRE on-call pages via PagerDuty immediately; page escalation to Eng Director if service-impacting > 30m.
- Communicate to customers via Solutions if > 2% of active tenants affected for > 60m.

Pre-rollout checklist (must be green before Day 0):
- [ ] Release artifact hash posted to release artifact registry and signed
- [ ] Canary keys and rate-limits configured for us-west1
- [ ] Backup config for rollback nodes validated (image, network ACLs)
- [ ] Dashboards and alerts validated (test alert triggers to verify)
- [ ] Runbook printed to incident channel and on-call paged with release window
- [ ] Customer-facing comms draft (if needed) in draft state (Solutions)

During-rollout checklist (operational items):
- [ ] Confirm deployment completed to canary nodes (image ID, config flags)
- [ ] Confirm routing-policy split active and observed in metrics
- [ ] Monitor p99 and 5xx per 1m buckets; log anomalies for postmortem
- [ ] Capture sample traces for both successful and failed requests
- [ ] If promoting, ensure autoscaler headroom (min spare nodes = 2)

Post-rollout tasks (within 24–72h):
- [ ] Confirm final metrics are within SLOs for 72h window
- [ ] Flush/refresh any training/experiment caches that assume old runtime behavior
- [ ] Create follow-up tickets for performance regressions or opt-in feature rollouts
- [ ] Schedule a 1-week post-launch retro (include SRE, runtime eng, product)

Postmortem triggers:
- Any full-region rollback triggered
- Customer-impacting outage > 30m or > 2% tenants affected
- New regressions that require a hotfix rollout

Open questions / unresolved: (short list)
- Should we run asia-northeast1 at a different time-of-day to align engineers — suggestion: schedule for early UTC morning to catch local daytime? (assigned to Aiko)
- Do we need a separate canary key set for enterprise tenants to avoid leakage? (assigned to Joanna)
- Contingency for cross-region KV cache warm-up time (could cause transient latency) — need exact warm-up numbers from Luca.

Appendix (quick commands & snippets):
- Promote traffic: `redwoodctl routing set canary --region us-west1 --percent 5`
- Rollback region: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --region us-west1 --image v2.13`
- Canary logs tail: `rb logs -f --service serving-runtime --region us-west1 --since 30m`

Notes: keep this doc short and operational. Longer postmortem and runbook details will live in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-ROLL/heatmap-2026). Current draft intentionally conservative on thresholds; fine-tune after staging dry-run on 2026-07-08.

End of document.
